text:
ashley: quick thread to align on upgrade experience and the lightweight migration tooling we promised customers. want a single crisp sentence for docs: what do we guarantee in v1?

pe ter: sorry small typo, peter here 

peter: tech POV: v1 guarantees: installer with offline bundle, private control plane with KMS integration, and a tenant gateway that provides outbound NAT. we DO NOT guarantee preserved customer IPs or seamless BGP peering on day 1.

jenny: field note: a few large customers will push hard on ip preservation. can we offer a documented migration path (not a turning-on-legs solution) and a dry-run mode? if yes, that should calm renewals.

ashley: agreed. suggestion: ship an "ip-migrate" CLI in alpha that offers a dry-run (report only) and a forced-migrate mode later. call out known caveats (ARP/conntrack resets).

peter: work plan sketch:
- ip-migrate report mode: analyze current endpoints and NAT mappings, estimate collision risk
- opt-in migration: drain flows, reassign VIPs, replay ARP where possible
- rollback: snapshot routing + NAT state before changes
We can ship report mode in 2 sprints. opt-in migration 3-4 additional sprints.

kai: security ask: any migration must preserve TLS cert continuity. doc the cert rotation steps and require customers to provide cert TTL policy during dry-run.

jenny: support asks for an automated collector and an escalations playbook. example command for collector: 
```
redwood-net-gather --tenant TENANT_ID --scope full --out /var/tmp/tenant-123.tgz
```
include collector output checklist in KB.

ashley: for launch comms we need a short customer promise line. proposal: "V1: private deploys with predictable control-plane upgrades, documented migration tooling; IP-preservation available as an opt-in migration in a later release." feedback?

peter: one more technical constraint: to keep installer simple we will default installer flag --preserve-ips=false. advanced customers can enable the migration workflow post-install. makes validation simpler.

jenny: customer-facing SLA language suggestion: "planned control-plane updates target <10 minutes of application-affecting change; emergency fixes may require longer windows and explicit coordination."

kai: also include guidance on required firewall/conntrack settings: recommend conntrack timeout >= 60s during migration and note that some appliances will drop ephemeral sessions. add this to KB.

ops-bot: scheduled task created: ip-migrate/report P0 -> staging on 1758004600

peter: roll-forward/rollback checklist (draft):
1) pre-check: run redwood-net-gather and ip-migrate --report
2) snapshot control plane DB
3) enable canary on 1% tenants for 24h, monitor pkg latency, egress error rate
4) run opt-in migration for selected tenants
5) if >2% increase in egress errors or >50 conntrack resets/min, trigger rollback
I'll fill numeric thresholds in the doc.

jenny: I'll prep a one-pager for account teams that explains the migration phases and expected timelines. include a short FAQ: why not IP-preserve GA? (BGP/peering complexity, proprietary firewalls, ARP nuances).

ashley: action items:
- peter: deliver ip-migrate report mode PR + README (due in 10 business days)
- kai: cert continuity checklist + firewall guidance (due EOD next Tue)
- jenny: customer one-pager + KB template (due next Fri)
- ashley: update launch page copy and renewal talking points (due next Wed)

ashley: thanks all 44d we keep the minimal path and promise an opt-in migration later. meeting to finalize the public wording Thursday 10am.
